subject: monsterTruck
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: monster truck with huge tyres.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
I'm checking the renders for proportion issues, noticing that the engine blower on the hood appears to overlap and block the windshield area in the front view.

Then I'm looking at the side render, which seems broken — mostly empty with only glowing or unpainted parts visible, as if the painted body parts aren't rendering from that camera angle, possibly a backface culling or material visibility issue.

Checking the other elements: exhaust stacks and flame cones look fine as salmon-toned cones, wheel textures seem reasonable, and the front view shows a good monster-truck proportion with narrow body against wide tire track.

Cab windshield, roof visor, and hood placement all check out, and the checkered flag positioning is fine too. The main issue I'm spotting is tire darkness—the treads read too uniformly black, so I want to lighten the tire palette with a brighter set of grays and add lug highlights for more readability.

Now I'm checking the body mud line and flame overlay positioning, the rear bed walls, and the bumper trim, which all look fine. The bigger concern is scale: the truck feels too small relative to the pad, so I'm tightening the pad dimensions and considering shifting the car forward to balance the composition.

I'm double-checking the stance: wheel radius plus lug clearance puts the bottom right near the pad surface, and the total height works out fine. I'll keep additional feature ideas minimal — maybe a door decal — and focus the fix list on three things: lowering/moving the engine forward so the windshield reads clearly, brightening the tire palette for visible tread, and refining the exhaust flame effect.

Taller stacked cone flames in yellow-orange with adjusted glow strength should read more convincingly, and I want to add door seams, handles, and possibly 4X4 decals using thin boxes positioned along the cab sides.

The door seams overlap the name text, so I'll skip doors entirely. I'm also checking mud flaps and fender flares behind the rear wheels, but since the tyre and bumper positions don't overlap, I'll skip those too — same with ramps or extra pads, not worth the complexity here.

I'll keep the edit list tight: reposition the engine block, adjust the tire palette, add flame exhaust and dust/steam effects, and leave the headlights as-is since they're close enough to glowing. For the engine, I'm repositioning the hood block, blower, and intake stacks slightly higher and forward for a more aggressive stance.

Adjusting pulley, belt, and windshield placement so the engine stays visible beneath the hood opening without clipping into the windshield slope.

Now I'm swapping the exhaust lines for taller flame stacks and building layered glow cones for the flame effect, nesting outer, inner, and tip cone colors at the stack top to create a gradient fire look.
